name: Kom
confidence_why: one confirmed first-hand source; 7 other works read were silent
catalog_citation: Shultz, George. 1997. Kom Language Grammar Sketch, Part 1. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research (Republic of Cameroon). 41 pp. (open PDF, sil.org via archived copy (Internet Archive, 2023))
catalog_locator: §2.2 Suprasegmental phonemes, printed p. 5 (PDF page 6 of 42; footer 'G. Shultz, SIL page 5 of 41')
catalog_quote: Kom is a tonal language. There are three level tones (high, mid, low) and three primary contour tones (low-falling, high-low, high-mid). Other contour tones rarely occur as a result of tone modification within the phrase. Only low and high-low tones are marked in the orthography. Vowel lengthening occasionally occurs in conjunction with a high-low tone or an emphatic utterance. This is not marked separately from the high-low tone mark. Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.citation: Shultz, George. 1997. Kom Language Grammar Sketch, Part 1. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research (Republic of Cameroon). 41 pp.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (42 pp. footer "G. Shultz, SIL.. page 5 of 41" on PDF page 6). The text layer is codepoint-shifted by +1 (raw: "Rsqdrr hr gd`qc nmkx hm dlog`shb roddbg ats hr mns l`qjdc-"); I decoded it independently and also rendered PDF page 6 to PNG (110 dpi) and read the image. §2.2 "Suprasegmental phonemes" reads exactly as quoted, all seven sentences, ending "Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked." Verbatim confirmed at the stated locator (§2.2, printed p. 5 = PDF p. 6). Reading: Kom is described as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L; contours low-falling, high-low, high-mid) with tone modification within the phrase; the only stress remark is that stress is heard only in…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kom is a three-level-tone language (H, M, L plus contour tones) with lexical and grammatical tone; there is no lexical or positional word stress. Perceptible stress occurs only as a feature of emphatic speech and is not. No position for stress is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the only qualification is that stress (and vowel lengthening) can be heard in emphatic utterances.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the language in general (suprasegmental phonemes); stress is tied to emphatic utterances, i.e. a pragmatic/phrase-level phenomenon, not the phonological word. Corroborated by Shultz 1993 (phonology notes, 23 pp.), Hyman 1984 (tonology ms., 95 sheets) and Kawuldim 2008 (§1.5), none of which mentions stress at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Shultz 1997 describes the main Kom dialect (Itaŋikom), which he says serves 95% of speakers; Mbesa and Ake village varieties are noted as closely related. All sources are for Kom of Boyo Division, Northwest Cameroon = komc1235 [bkm]; Bruens's 'Nkom' is the same language under an older name.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item and it was opened and checked in full above, so there was nothing marked silent-unopened to spot-check. As an extra spot-check I a full-text search for stress/accent the other on-disk Kom sources in the folder (Hyman 1984 Kom Tonology scanned, Chia & Kimbi 1992 alphabet guide scanned, Kawuldim 2008 thesis text, Shultz 1997 decoded text) for stress|accent|prominen|emphat: the only hits are Shultz 1997 §2.2 p. 5 ('Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked.'), which is already the catalog's existing statement, and unrelated 'emphatic subject/particle' glosses in Kawuldim. Nothing missed.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 1984 [posted 2019]. Kom Tonology. Unpublished manuscript, University of California, Berkeley. 95 sheets.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Detailed nominal tonology: surface H, M, L, L' (non-downgliding L) analysed as underlying /H/ and /L/ with floating tones and spreading. scanned of all 95 sheets: no occurrence of stress/accent/prominence.

sources.citation: Shultz, George (1993). Notes on the phonology of the Kom language. SIL. SIL Cameroon. 22 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Same language as the catalog (Kom, SIL Cameroon field research June 1989 to March 1991, research assistant Pius Loh). The work says nothing on stress; its three-level-plus-contour tone description is fully compatible with the existing statement from Shultz 1997 §2.2 ("Kom is a tonal language.. Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked"), which is by the same author and supersedes this 1993 tentative sketch on that point.

sources.note: Tertiary: 'Kom is a tonal language with three tones'; eight phonetic tones, two marked. No stress statement. Used only to recover the current sil.org URLs of the Shultz 1993/1997, Kawuldim 2008 and Chia & Kimbi 1992 PDFs.

sources.citation: Kawuldim, Kimbi Paul. 2008. Relativization in Kom. MA thesis, Nairobi Evangelical Graduate School of Theology. xiv+81 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1.5 Phonology and Orthography (pp. 3-4): 'Kom is a tonal language.. There are three tones, high, low and falling but only two tones are marked'; tone occurs on all syllables and is contrastive. Nothing on stress (only a remark that intonation rises on the question tag a, p. 35).

sources.citation: Shultz, George. 1993 (June). Notes on the Phonology of the Kom Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 22 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Whole paper is phonology (23-page scan, scanned). §8 Tone (pp. 14-15): eight phonetic pitches, three level (H, M, L) and five contour; lexical and grammatical tone; downstep. §4 Word structure: words of 1-4 syllables, monosyllables most frequent. No mention of stress or accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned: no hits).
